item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because its production code is effectively identical to A’s, while its tests more directly exercise the new Upload API, multipart content, and an end-to-end 429 retry.","reasons":["B verifies the multipart field, filename, and actual uploaded content; A never asserts the file content.","B tests retries through FilesService.Upload itself, whereas A only adds a generic retry-transport test using a bytes.Reader.","Both correctly reuse multipartbody.NewFile and preserve the existing Add signature.","Both violate the explicit contract to route Upload through FilesService.Add: they duplicate Add’s option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...)."],"risks_a":["No Upload-level retry test, so the reported regression is not directly covered.","Multipart testing omits the uploaded content assertion.","No tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures despite the contract requiring them."],"risks_b":["The retry test does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true, so it does not precisely reproduce the reported configuration.","The retry source is strings.Reader rather than an intentionally non-seekable reader, weakening proof of streamed-source replayability.","No tests for empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures despite the contract requiring them."]}
